medium.en: Hanging scroll; ink and colour on paper

institution.name: The Metropolitan Museum of Art
institution.credit_line: Gift of Marie-Hélène and Guy Weill, in honor of Wen C. Fong, 2015

image.edit: Trimmed the dark photographic background around the object, then resized.

basis.en: Public domain: the artist died in 1559. The Metropolitan Museum of Art releases this image under CC0 through its Open Access programme.
basis.zh: 公有领域：作者卒于 1559 年。大都会艺术博物馆通过开放获取计划以 CC0 发布此图像。

alt.en: A pale landscape in soft colour. A two-storey pavilion stands among tall pines and leafless trees, with two figures seated in the open upper room; a gate and a path lie below, mountains rise in mist behind, and a long inscription in neat script fills the top of the scroll.
alt.zh: 一幅淡设色的山水。一座两层的楼阁立在高松和落叶的树之间，敞开的楼上坐着两个人；下方有门和小径，身后的山在雾中升起，画幅上部写满了工整的长题。

note.en: Wen Zhengming painted this at seventy-three for an old friend, Master Liu, who longed to live in an upper-storey retreat, above the dust of the world and among his books. Wen’s poem at the top speaks of the wish. It is less a landscape than a portrait of a reading room, and a fitting picture for a library that also lives a little above the street.
note.zh: 文徵明七十三岁时为老友刘先生画了这幅画——刘先生一直向往住进一座楼居，高出尘世，与书为伴。顶上文徵明的诗写的就是这份心愿。与其说这是山水，不如说是一间读书楼的肖像；挂在一座也稍稍高于街市的图书馆里，正合适。
